Definition: a prolonged form of a primary but defective verb εἵλω (of the same meaning); to coil or wrap:--roll together. See also G1667.
BiblicalUsage: Heilisso means to roll together, to coil up like a scroll, and it appears once, at the end of the world as John sees it. In Revelation 6:14 the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together, and every mountain and island is moved out of its place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is meant to frighten and to comfort at once: the sky itself is rolled up like a finished letter, and the God who wrote it is the one who closes it.
